quotes.speaker: Michael C. Wright
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael C. Wright on the Hoop Collective visiting the Philippines
quotes.excerpt: I am super excited for you guys as a Filipino, I have never been to the Philippines.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael C. Wright
text_blocks.text: I am super excited for you guys as a Filipino, I have never been to the Philippines. My mom is from Cebu City, but I have already told Tim MacMahon, because I heard a previous podcast where he said, 'I am an adventurous eater.' Okay, you are adventurous, you need to try balut. Do you know what balut is, Tim?

text_blocks.speaker: Michael C. Wright
text_blocks.text: It is a duck egg that has been incubated like 21 days and they sort of like pickle it in vinegar and stuff and you just crack the shell. My mom told me that dudes at the bar, that is what they eat. And so I hit Timmy up and I was like, 'Hey, since you are so adventurous, you should try balut.'

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: He is definitely a dude at the bar.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on rejecting a team dinner location in Melbourne
quotes.excerpt: Jackson sent me a menu of a possible place for a team dinner in Melbourne and I rejected it.
quotes.quote: Jackson sent me a menu of a possible place for a team dinner in Melbourne and I rejected it. Why is that? Because it did not have chicken parm on there. First off, the Australians are known for their parms, their parmies, and you can get one on every corner. And that I would be sent a menu that did not have a parmie is right out of the gate, we are in trouble. But I approve the second one, MacMahon, that you have not been advised.

quotes.speaker: Michael C. Wright
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael C. Wright on missing the Spurs media day meeting
quotes.excerpt: I ended up getting to miss that because I was at Rockets media day.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael C. Wright
text_blocks.text: What happened during the meeting? Because I ended up getting to miss that because I was at Rockets media day.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: They said you are going to be working. That is the Cliff Notes version.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael C. Wright
text_blocks.text: What is new? What is new?

quotes.speaker: Michael C. Wright
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael C. Wright on Victor Wembanyama's reaction to the playoffs
quotes.excerpt: I am hearing that Victor does not want to talk about what happened in the finals.
quotes.quote: I am hearing that Victor does not want to talk about what happened in the finals. I am hearing he is like locked in. As a matter of fact, I was told that he has not even, he is not even talking to any American media outlets except for 60 Minutes.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on the Spurs' lack of leadership regarding Wembanyama
quotes.excerpt: You cannot hit a guy in the throat, I don't care if it's in October.
quotes.quote: You cannot hit a guy in the throat, I don't care if it's in October, and you sure as bleep cannot do it in the playoffs. You cannot do it. And then take zero accountability. The Spurs helped him out on that. And the Spurs, you know, for all this, for all this, you know, the leadership of the organization, I did not sense an incredible amount of leadership on the Spurs organization. And look, they got to, they got to manage Wembanyama, but I did not, you know, Popovich can meet him, can meet people at the at the airport, you know, Tim Duncan can pull people aside. You got to get the results of that. It is not defined. I mean, Victor has got 20 years left, but I did not think that their Spurs leadership on that was, was exemplary, that is all I will say.

quotes.speaker: Michael C. Wright
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael C. Wright on the Spurs' rigorous postseason compared to the Knicks
quotes.excerpt: There is that belief that, you know, as the Spurs, they went through sort of a more rigorous postseason.
quotes.quote: There is that belief that, you know, as the Spurs, they went through sort of a more rigorous postseason than the New York Knicks. And by the time they got to the finals, you know, just sort of the emotional stuff, all that stuff really wore them down going into that series, meanwhile the Knicks basically steamrolled everybody after that first round.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim MacMahon on the Spurs' philosophy of deferring to Wembanyama
quotes.excerpt: The philosophy is whatever Wemby wants is what we are going to do.
quotes.quote: The philosophy is whatever Wemby wants is what we are going to do. And I get it, he is just such an incredible talent and is so focused and determined and you know, just wants to pour everything he possibly can into maximizing his potential. But there, you know, there is a little bit of, you know, he needs some guidance, I would say. He needs still needs some guidance, but listen, he also does things like walks into a hostile arena in Oklahoma City for Game 1 of the Western Conference Finals and has one of the most incredible playoff performances I have ever seen with my own eyes and goes back there for a Game 7 and closes out the series.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on LeBron James' first finals appearance
quotes.excerpt: LeBron's first finals, it was the men versus the boys against San Antonio.
quotes.quote: LeBron's first finals, it was the men versus the boys against San Antonio and LeBron was not ready for it. He was not, he was not at the top. Kobe had Shaq in his prime. I mean, the Kobe that led them to the three straight finals, post-Shaq, with you know, him screaming at Pau Gasol and Lamar Odom and Andrew Bynum up and down the court, that was a, I am just saying, that Kobe did not pop out at age 21. The LeBron who carried the Cavs to the 2016 finals, it was a different LeBron James when he was 21, okay? I think he was 22 when he went to the finals for the first time.

quotes.speaker: Michael C. Wright
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael C. Wright on the Spurs' expansion and tryouts
quotes.excerpt: They are trying to get 100 new members.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael C. Wright
text_blocks.text: They are trying to get 100 new members. I went to the tryouts the other day and it was wild. I I have to look through my phone notes because I kind of took notes just to get color just in case I write about it at some point. But I know I spotted at least four or five dudes with like full-blown green alien suits.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim MacMahon on Dylan Harper's future role
quotes.excerpt: By the way, another guy you are going to be writing about is Dylan Harper.
quotes.quote: By the way, another guy you are going to be writing about is Dylan Harper.

quotes.speaker: Michael C. Wright
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael C. Wright on Julian Champagnie's playing time
quotes.excerpt: I am guessing that Julian isn't going to start anymore.
quotes.quote: Like a guy like Julian Champagnie, he is starting, he set a record for threes in the season. And then you bring in Tobias Harris and I am guessing that Julian isn't going to start anymore.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim MacMahon on the Spurs' starting lineup challenges
quotes.excerpt: And that is not the biggest issue with the starting lineup.
quotes.quote: And that is not the biggest issue with the starting lineup. And you know, this is a thing like you have got a young coach who, you know, it was a rough final series but did a hell of a job in his first full year as a coach. But listen man, Dylan Harper, number two overall pick, had a great rookie year in a limited role coming off the bench. And like it is no secret, he is not going to be satisfied coming off the bench. The people in his camp are not going to be happy if he is coming off the bench.

quotes.speaker: Michael C. Wright
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael C. Wright on the Spurs' roster development
quotes.excerpt: All the talent I have got on this roster, I have crazy ideas that I want to implement.
quotes.quote: All the talent I have got on this roster, I have crazy ideas that I want to implement. But you really cannot implement those ideas if you do not have the time to rep them, you know, in practice. I think maybe there is a chance they go in and aggregators leave me alone. But there is a chance going in that all three of those guards could start.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim MacMahon on the Spurs' three-guard lineup shooting issues
quotes.excerpt: One of the challenges with playing those three guards together is none of the three are good shooters.
quotes.quote: One of the challenges with playing those three guards together is none of the three are good three-point shooters. And so the like the shooting could become challenging. Although listen, you always give room for like maybe Harper or Castle came, you know, had a great summer working on their shot and then makes a leap like you see guys improve as three-point shooters early in their careers all the time.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on the Spurs' internal view of Devin Vassell
quotes.excerpt: The Spurs internally believe Devin Vassell is their second best player.
quotes.quote: The Spurs internally believe Devin Vassell is their second best player. I am not saying Mitch Johnson is going to come out and say that, he should not come out and say that, that is not a slight on De'Aaron Fox, that is not a slight on Stefan Castle. Vassell is a stud. You talk to other front offices in the league, they say the same thing. This guy is, I mean look, he is a number two pick in the draft, of course he is a stud. Of course he is a stud and he only got better as the season went along.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on Tobias Harris as an ego-less player
quotes.excerpt: Tobias Harris, definitely an ego-less guy, veteran ego-less guy, great signing.
quotes.quote: Tobias Harris, definitely an ego-less guy, veteran ego-less guy, great signing, 15 million a year for two years, ego-less. So, it helps, I think that you are going to have two guys who potentially have to have their their their roles limited who I think will be open to doing that.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on Fred VanVleet's impact on the Rockets
quotes.excerpt: Fred VanVleet is back and to me, like it is Fred VanVleet is back period.
quotes.quote: Fred VanVleet is back and to me, like it is Fred VanVleet is back period and then start everything else because no matter what anybody wants to say, no matter what Reed Shepherd's mustache and hair look like, no matter what Amen Thompson has signed his contract, Fred VanVleet coming back is one of the, if we are going to talk about this division, it might be one of the headlines in the division.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim MacMahon on Kevin Durant's impact on the Rockets' issues
quotes.excerpt: Kevin Durant was part of both of those problems.
quotes.quote: Kevin Durant was part of both of those problems. I would say you you could even say Kevin Durant was at the top of the list of both of those problems. At the same time, KD was kind of thrust into, I am not going to say unfair, but a a position that didn't play to his strengths, having to be the primary initiator, down to stretch the games, having to be um the the default leader, the guy most responsible for the mood of the locker room. Those don't play to his strengths. Those do play to Fred VanVleet's strengths and and kind of takes those burdens off of KD's shoulders this year.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on Kyrie Irving's availability for the Mavericks
quotes.excerpt: Is this a team that Kyrie Irving is going to be on when we get to February?
quotes.quote: Is this a team that Kyrie Irving is going to be on when we get to February? That is what that is what the league is is watching. Absolutely. And uh you know, Messiah did not want to have any discussions about Kyrie trades this year. I you know, what I can tell you right now is Kyrie is fully on board and excited about coming back to play with the Mavericks.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on the Pelicans' lack of tanking last season
quotes.excerpt: The Pelicans were not tanking last year because they didn't have their pick.
quotes.quote: The Pelicans were not tanking last year because they didn't have their pick. Because it is a devastating stat, okay? The Pelicans were not tanking last year because they didn't have their pick. They went nine and 45 against teams 500 and above. That is just unfortunately not competitive.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Cameron Boozer's role in the Grizzlies' starting lineup
quotes.excerpt: Cameron Boozer will be in their starting lineup to start the season and for a long time

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: I know one guy for sure who is going to be in their starting lineup, he wears number 27.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: Cameron Boozer will be in their starting lineup to start the season and for a long time to come. He is their new franchise guy. Obviously this is all health pending. Zach Edey will start at the five.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Cedric Howard's starting role over Jeremy Grant
quotes.excerpt: Cedric Howard is going to start ahead of Jeremy Grant

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Cedric Howard is going to start ahead of Jeremy Grant, I am sorry Jeremy.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: Cedric Howard will also start ahead of Jeremy Grant. They really, really, really like Howard. He was their first-round pick in 25.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Grizzlies' developmental year and future cap space strategy
quotes.excerpt: The Grizzlies are a team to watch. This year is a developmental year with the young guys
quotes.quote: The Grizzlies are a team to watch. This year is a developmental year with the young guys and then in the summer, they have a chance to be very aggressive in the trade market and or look for them to be a team that tries to poach restricted free agents again. With these second aprons, there are going to be tough decisions or there are going to be talented players that move teams in restricted free agency in the years to come.

quotes.speaker: Michael Wright
quotes.summary_phrase: The impact of moving on from Ja Morant
quotes.excerpt: They really had to move on from Ja just so Tomas Satoransky could have a clean slate

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Wright
text_blocks.text: You almost feel like they really had to move on from Ja just so Tomas Satoransky could have a clean slate and a real chance to implement what he is doing with these young guys. I think it is going to be unconventional. Would you agree on that, Tim?

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: I would say he is known for being unconventional. But yeah, obviously it was just time for Ja to get a second chance somewhere else because it was not going to work out in Memphis and the Grizzlies needed him to be gone just to have a chance to completely turn the page and so begins the Cam Boozer era.
